All development is tracked in Jira. The board is the only status source (delivery plan section 1).

| | |
|---|---|
| Site | `57blocks.atlassian.net` |
| Project | `AN` (Anifit), team-managed |
| Board | [1144](https://57blocks.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/AN/boards/1144/backlog) |
| Issue types | Epic, Story, Task, Bug, Subtask |
| Access for agents | The `atlassian` MCP server in `.mcp.json`. Each person signs in with their own Atlassian account: run `/mcp`, select `atlassian`, then authorize in the browser |

### Issue types

| Type | Use it for | Parent |
|---|---|---|
| Epic | One week of work, Monday to Friday. Name: `W<two-digit week> <short theme>`, for example `W01 Foundations` (AN-1). Set Start date and Due date to the Monday and the Friday | None |
| Story | One deliverable of the week. This includes technical work, for example CI, infrastructure or a plan | The Epic of the week |
| Task | Small work that is not a deliverable, for example a configuration change or a chore | The Epic of the week |
| Bug | A behavior that does not agree with the acceptance criterion or the design | The Epic of the week in which it is fixed |
| Subtask | One step of a Story, Task or Bug | Story, Task or Bug |

Work that is not done by Friday moves to the Epic of the next week.

### Fields

- **Summary.** Short, in English, in the imperative. A Story that covers acceptance criteria puts their IDs at the end, for example `Offer the allowed payment methods at checkout (A2-AC-006)`.
- **Parent.** Every Story, Task and Bug has the Epic of its week as parent.
- **Description.** Use the template below.
- **Labels.**
  - The release: `R0`, `R0.x`, `RC` or `R1`.
  - The module, for Stories, Tasks and Bugs in one module: `mod-identity`, `mod-commerce`, `mod-subscription`, `mod-commission`, `mod-journey`, `mod-content`, `mod-ai`, `mod-integration` or `mod-kernel` ([architecture section 4](architecture.md#4-modules)). Work across modules, such as CI or planning, has no module label.

- **Story point estimate.** The team sets it in sprint planning. Do not set it unless asked.

```markdown
## Context
Why this work is necessary. One to three sentences.

## Scope
- What is included.
- What is not included.

## Acceptance criteria
- A2-AC-006 (the ID only. `pnpm ids show A2-AC-006` prints the text).

## Sources
- Discovery item IDs, ADRs, design links.
```

A Story also lists its annex items and its inputs (definition of ready, delivery plan section 9). An Epic uses the sections Goal, Exit and Sources.

### Rules for agents

- Read before you write. Search with JQL for an issue that already exists before you create a new one.
- Before you create, change or transition more than one issue, show the list to the user and get approval.
- Do not delete issues. Do not change the status of an issue that another person owns, unless the user asks.

- Name the issue key in the branch name and in the pull request title, for example branch `AN-123-paypal-checkout` and title `feat: pay an order with PayPal (AN-123)`.

# Module `identity`

## Owns

The person record with roles (T3-D-009), credentials, sessions, consents, preferences, pets, consultations. PostgreSQL schema `identity`.

## Public API (`index.ts`) <!-- verified: exports -->

| Export | Use |
|---|---|
| `createIdentity({ repo, bus, clock })` | Builds the module service |
| `.registerPerson({ email, givenName, familyName, brand? })` | Creates a person. Publishes `identity.person-registered` |
| `.getPerson(id)` | Reads a person or `null` |
| `InMemoryPersonRepository` | Store for tests and the fixture |
| `EmailAlreadyRegisteredError` | Thrown when the e-mail exists |
| `Identity`, `IdentityDeps`, `RegisterPersonInput` | Types of the service |
| `Person`, `PersonRepository`, `PersonRegistered` | Types of the record, the store and the event |

## Tables (`schema.ts`)

| Table | Personal columns |
|---|---|
| `identity.person` | `email`, `given_name`, `family_name` |

## Events <!-- verified: events -->

| Event | Direction | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `identity.person-registered` | Emits | `personId`, `brand` |

## Invariants

- One person record per e-mail address. The e-mail is stored in lower case (T3-AC-003).
- At most one ERP customer number per person (T3-AC-003).
- ERP master data comes through the `integration` module, never from the ERP port.

## Acceptance criteria

T3-AC-003, T3-AC-004.

1	# Data conventions
2	
3	Source: [architecture.md section 5](../architecture.md#5-data), ADR-0011, TD-09.
4	
5	## Tables
6	
7	- Each module owns one PostgreSQL schema. Define tables in `packages/core/src/<module>/schema.ts` with Drizzle.
8	- A module never reads another module's tables. Use the other module's public API.
9	- **Every table is wrapped in `withDataMeta(table, meta)`** from `kernel`. `meta` has one entry per column.
10	- A column that is not personal data: `notPersonal`.
11	- A personal data column:
12	
13	  ```ts
14	  phone: {
15	    personal: true,
16	    category: "contact",           // contact | identity | preference | financial | health | other
17	    purpose: "Contact about an order",            // why the platform keeps it
18	    owner: "identity",             // the module that owns it
19	    retention: "account lifetime + 3 years",          // how long the platform keeps it
20	  },
21	  ```
22	
23	- Personal data is any value that identifies a person or is about a person: names, e-mail, phone, address, date of birth, bank details, IP address, consent choices.
24	- `pnpm pii` fails when a column has no metadata, when a personal column has an empty purpose, owner or retention, or when a column name shows personal data but the metadata says `personal: false`.
25	- Default retention for account data: `account lifetime + 3 years`. Consent records: `account lifetime + 3 years` (proof of consent).
26	
27	## Values
28	
29	- **Money** is an integer in minor units with a currency: `kernel.money(amountMinor)`. Never a float.
30	- **Time** is stored in UTC as an ISO string. A business date uses the `Europe/Berlin` calendar: `kernel.businessDate(instant)`.
31	- **IDs** are UUIDv7: `kernel.newId(now)`. ERP keys (customer number `K123456`, advisor number `B12345`) are separate columns.
32	- **Brand**: entities that a second brand would split have a `brand` column (T3-D-013).

# Data conventions

Source: [architecture.md section 5](../architecture.md#5-data), ADR-0011, TD-09.

## Tables

- Each module owns one PostgreSQL schema. Define tables in `packages/core/src/<module>/schema.ts` with Drizzle.
- A module never reads another module's tables. Use the other module's public API.
- **Every table is wrapped in `withDataMeta(table, meta)`** from `kernel`. `meta` has one entry per column.
- A column that is not personal data: `notPersonal`.
- A personal data column:

  ```ts
  phone: {
    personal: true,
    category: "contact",           // contact | identity | preference | financial | health | other
    purpose: "Contact about an order",            // why the platform keeps it
    owner: "identity",             // the module that owns it
    retention: "account lifetime + 3 years",          // how long the platform keeps it
  },
  ```

- Personal data is any value that identifies a person or is about a person: names, e-mail, phone, address, date of birth, bank details, IP address, consent choices.
- `pnpm pii` fails when a column has no metadata, when a personal column has an empty purpose, owner or retention, or when a column name shows personal data but the metadata says `personal: false`.
- Default retention for account data: `account lifetime + 3 years`. Consent records: `account lifetime + 3 years` (proof of consent).

## Values

- **Money** is an integer in minor units with a currency: `kernel.money(amountMinor)`. Never a float.
- **Time** is stored in UTC as an ISO string. A business date uses the `Europe/Berlin` calendar: `kernel.businessDate(instant)`.
- **IDs** are UUIDv7: `kernel.newId(now)`. ERP keys (customer number `K123456`, advisor number `B12345`) are separate columns.
- **Brand**: entities that a second brand would split have a `brand` column (T3-D-013).

I stopped before writing any code. Three things block a pull request-ready change here:

1. **No Jira story key.** The repo's workflow starts every change with `/story-start AN-<n>`, which writes `docs/specs/AN-<n>/spec.md` and `plan.md`. The branch name and the PR title (`feat: … (AN-<n>)`) also need the key. I can't make one up, and the Jira rules say to look for an existing issue before creating one.
2. **No acceptance criterion ID.** Hard rule 5 says every test title must start with the ID of the acceptance criterion it covers, and rule 6 forbids inventing IDs. I searched the docs and the Discovery register for "birth" and found nothing about a person's date of birth. The only hits are journey triggers ("customer or pet birthday") and the PII convention.
3. **I can't run shell commands in this session.** That means no `pnpm check`, which the repo says must pass, no `pnpm ids show`, no tests and no commit or push. So I can't verify the change or get it to a PR.

**What I found so far:** this should be a normal story, not a design story. It adds a column to an existing table, and the new personal data uses the existing `identity` category in `packages/core/src/identity/schema.ts`. It changes no event or module boundary, so it needs no ADR and no second-person approval.

The planned change:
- **Data:** a `date_of_birth` column, `personal: true`, category `identity`, owner `identity`, retention `account lifetime + 3 years`.
- **Code:** `registerPerson` gets an optional ISO `dateOfBirth`. It rejects a badly formatted date and a date after today in the `Europe/Berlin` calendar, using the injected clock. The new error is exported from `index.ts`.
- **Read:** `getPerson` returns `dateOfBirth` or `null`.
- **Docs:** the module `AGENTS.md` lists the new input field, column, error and invariant.

**To go on, I need:**
- The Jira key (AN-<n>) for this story, or your approval to create one under the current week's Epic.
- Which acceptance criterion ID it covers. If there is none, someone has to add one to the Discovery register; I can't invent it.
- Shell access (Bash) for `pnpm`, so I can run `pnpm check` and commit, or tell me you'll run those yourself.
